_provenance.approved_by: Andrew, 2026-09-15 — reviewed against the rule set, no vetoes
_provenance.why: Rotation A ran Aug 24 – Sep 14. Andrew: 'my family doesn't want to eat those same 8 meals again for the next two weeks.'
_provenance.SOURCED: the household rule set, the portion table, the store section order, and the three keeper meals — all carried unchanged from fuel-seed.json
_provenance.INFERRED: every qty_per_person for vegetables, starches, aromatics and seasonings in the five NEW meals. Protein weights come from the portion table and are NOT inferred. Same convention as rotation A: inferred rows render as 'est.' in the UI and get corrected in the aisle.
_provenance.design_note: A meal belongs to MANY rotations — three meals are in both A and B. Rotation membership is therefore a join, not a column on fuel_meals. Week number moves out of rotation_note prose and becomes data.
_provenance.macros: carbs_g_per_person, fat_g_per_person and calories_per_person are NULL on all five new meals (FOR-234 SS4, shape only), same as the eight in fuel-seed.json. scripts/fuel-seed-sql.mjs throws on a meal MISSING a macro key and throws again on a meal carrying a VALUE — the keys must be present and null until a seed migration carries them. Corrected 2026-09-15 after CC found them absent: they were absent because this fixture was drafted against a checkout 77 commits behind origin/master, where FOR-234 had not landed.

fuel_rotations.name: Fortnight One
fuel_rotations.note: The original eight. Ran Aug 24 – Sep 14, 2026.

fuel_rotations.name: Fortnight Two
fuel_rotations.note: Five new meals plus the three keepers. Same cut mix as rotation A — ribeye 1, chicken thigh 2, ground turkey 2, fish 2, chicken breast 1 — so the Costco shop is identical in shape and cost. Every spice profile and format is new against rotation A.

fuel_meals_new.name: Miso-ginger glazed salmon, green beans, rice
fuel_meals_new.rotation_note: FISH — week 1. Bought fresh at Costco with the main shop, same slot as the lemon-garlic salmon it replaces. Glaze goes on before the broiler, so most of the clock is hands-off.

fuel_meals_new.name: Jerk chicken thighs, roasted sweet potato, broccoli
fuel_meals_new.rotation_note: Week 2. Same thigh as the chili-lime night, different profile and format — L5 in practice. 10 active minutes; the oven does the rest. Cooks 3 so a leftover night comes free.

fuel_meals_new.name: Turkey meatballs, tomato-basil, green beans
fuel_meals_new.rotation_note: TURKEY — week 2, in the slot the turkey burgers held. 93/7 ONLY — 99% lean will not hold a meatball together any better than it holds a patty. Reheats better than anything else in either rotation.

fuel_meals_new.name: Tandoori chicken breast, cucumber-tomato salad, rice
fuel_meals_new.rotation_note: Week 2. BREAST not thigh — deliberately, to keep a full pound of margin in the thigh bag, same reason as the stir-fry it replaces. Active time drops 25 → 15 because the marinade is passive. Marinate in the morning or the night before; total_minutes excludes the marinade.

fuel_meals_new.name: Chipotle-lime cod tacos, cabbage slaw
fuel_meals_new.rotation_note: FISH — week 2. BOUGHT ON THE SECOND TRIP, not the main shop — learning L3, same as the blackened cod it replaces. Cod is leaner than salmon, so weigh heavier. THE ONE DELIBERATE L5 EXCEPTION: corn tortillas and cabbage are bought for this meal and nothing else. Approved by Andrew 2026-09-15 on the grounds that it is the most different plate in the rotation and both items are cheap.

_rule_check._comment: Rotation B checked against fuel_household.dietary_rules. Every line measured from fuel_rotation_meals + fuel_meals, not asserted.
_rule_check.meals_per_fortnight: 8 — 4 keeper/new in week 1, 4 new in week 2
_rule_check.fish_per_week: 1 and 1 — miso salmon (wk1, main shop) and cod tacos (wk2, second trip)
_rule_check.ground_turkey_per_week: 1 and 1 — greek turkey bowl (wk1, keeper) and turkey meatballs (wk2). Both 93/7.
_rule_check.steak_per_month: 1 ribeye in rotation B. Running A then B in one month = exactly 2. At the cap, not over.
_rule_check.protein_floor_g_per_person: min 40 (cod tacos), max 48 (ribeye). Floor is 40. PASS.
_rule_check.cook_cap_minutes: max active is 20 (turkey meatballs). Rotation A's worst was 25. PASS.
_rule_check.wheelhouse_cuts_only: PASS — ribeye, thigh, breast, turkey 93/7, salmon, cod/halibut.
_rule_check.new_profiles_vs_rotation_a: miso-ginger, jerk, tomato-basil, tandoori-yogurt, chipotle-lime — none appear in rotation A.
_rule_check.new_formats_vs_rotation_a: broiled, oven-roast, meatball, marinate-and-broil, taco — none appear in rotation A.
_rule_check.frugal_reuse_L5: Held everywhere except chipotle-cod-tacos, which is a flagged and approved exception. Every other new ingredient (miso, jerk seasoning, tandoori seasoning, greek yogurt, crushed tomatoes, basil, egg) is a pantry or dairy staple that outlives the fortnight.
_rule_check.prep_diversion_pct: UNCHANGED at 50. Every meat quantity in this file is PER PERSON PER MEAL and must still be doubled at the shopping-list layer. This file does not apply the diversion.
